figures.caption: Supplementary Figure 5. SEM-EDX analysis of as-synthesized LPSCl1.5. The figures show the five selected areas and the Cl/P ratios are summarized in the table. Supplementary note 1. Calculation of the theoretical oxidation capacity of argyrodites. We performed SEM-EDX analysis as shown in Supplementary Figure 5, indicating the average Cl/P ratio is 1.1. We also calculated the lattice parameter of as-synthesized argyrodite which is a = 9.843 Å, lying between that of Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 (9.806 Å) and Li6PS5Cl (9.860 Å). Using the linear relationship between lattice parameter and x in the solid solution described by Li6-xPS5-xCl1+x, x = 1.1. Therefore, the as-synthesized LPSCl1.5 was corrected to an actual stoichiometry of LPSCl1.1 with a theoretical capacity of 280 mAh g-1. figures.label: S6
figures.caption: Supplementary Figure 6. a, Initial charge profile of pristine LPSCl1.5 cell at 0.15 mA cm-2; b, Corresponding differential capacity dQ/dV analysis. The cathode consists of only 70% LPSCl1.5 and 30% VC. Compared to the curves in Figure 2c-d and Wagemaker et. al.’s work,1 the shapes of the charge profiles and the differential capacity curves including the plateaus and peaks are almost identical. The observed peak shift is ascribed to the different active material content and chemical environment in the different cathodes. Therefore, the voltage plateau at 2.4 V must correspond to the first step in the oxidation process of the argyrodite as reported in ref. 1.

figures.label: S7
figures.caption: Supplementary Figure 7. Analysis of the initial charge process for three cells (VC/LPSC1.5, NG/LPSC1.5 and CNG/LPSC1.5). Taking the VC/LPSCl1.5 cell as an example – because this cell showed the highest oxidation capacity and each process is well distinguished – up to 2.96 V, 1.77 e- was consumed in the oxidation of the argyrodite, whereas 1.8 e- would be required based on our proposed process. Considering the total electrons consumed up to 4.1 V are 2.77 e-, and the theoretical would be 2.8 e-, the required coulomb capacity is in accord with our mechanism.

figures.label: S11
figures.caption: Supplementary Figure 11. Structural configurations displaying the relaxed structure after removing Li from the (top) LPSCl1.5_010 slab surface, (middle) LPSCl1.5|C interface, and (bottom) LPSCl1.5|C3N4 interface. Two Li vacancies are created in succession. Li atoms removed during vacancy formation are marked with black circles. Li that moved from the inner layer of LPSCl1.5 to the interface during DFT relaxation are marked with a red circle and represent Li-rich interfaces. To gauge the favourability of Li-N bonding at the interface, we conducted simulations involving the creation of a Li vacancy at the LPSCl1.5|CNG interface. This resulted in Li atoms from the adjacent layer of LPSCl1.5 diffusing to the interface, thus reinstating similar Li-N bonds and demonstrating the energetic favourability of such bonds at the interfaces.

figures.caption: Supplementary Figure 12. PBE-DFT calculated DOS for pristine LPSCl1.5 (a), graphene-LPSCl1.5 (b) and two configurations of C3N4-LPSCl1.5 (c & d) composite, respectively. We used PBE-DFT calculations to calculate total and atom-projected electronic density of states (DOS) for LPSCl1.5, graphene-LPSCl1.5, and C3N4-LPSCl1.5 to understand and compare the electronic transport at the interfaces. While PBE-DFT tends to underestimate band gaps, we focused on comparison of atom-projected and total DOS at various interfaces. figures.label: S17
figures.caption: Supplementary Figure 17. DRT analysis of the impedance of three cells (CNG 4.1 V, NG 4.1 V and VC 4.1 V) after argyrodite oxidation upon charging the cells to 4.1V. Two peaks correspond to the Li+ transport across the interphase and charge transfer within the cathode, respectively. The DRT results show the same trends as in Figure 2c- d, with a very large decrease in the peak intensity of the CNG cell compared to the NG and VC cells, indicating the smallest charge transfer resistance. The DRT provides additional proof that the oxidation of LPSCl1.5 is suppressed at the LPSCl1.5/CNG interface.

figures.label: S25
figures.caption: Supplementary Figure 25. Cycling performance of Li-In|LPSCl1.5|VC/S/LPSCl1.5 SSSBs with different cutoff voltages (2.7 V and 3.1 V) at room temperature. While it appears that the initial capacity of the VC cell is about the same if curtailed at 2.7 V (Fig 2a) as that for the CNG cell up to 3.1 V (Fig. 2b), the long-term cycling performance of the VC cell at that cutoff voltage is very poor. The oxidation of argyrodite starts below 2.6 V (for VC and NG; Figure 2c-d) and therefore a cutoff of 2.7 V will not completely inhibit decomposition. Clearly some oxidation of argyrodite occurs in Fig 2a even below 2.7 V, but it partially overlaps with the charge plateau.
